headline: Shared filesystem and shell-capable AutoGPT can collide with cognee’s tenant-scoped memory and sensitive data flows; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while cognee exposes CLI/API surfaces and session memory. A shared file or copied output could be treated as trusted input by either agent. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from documented surfaces rather than observed interaction.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or copied outputs are pasted between them, prompt content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
IF cognee ingests AutoGPT-generated text without provenance checks, injected directives can propagate.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of agent-generated files.
Add a provenance prefix to all inter-agent handoffs.
Review any copied text before pasting between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive content can flow from cognee into AutoGPT’s context and then out through its network path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so the risk is inferred and not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory, files containing personal or finance data can be read by AutoGPT.
IF AutoGPT forwards file contents to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of AutoGPT’s filesystem scope.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Block outbound access except to approved endpoints.
Redact personal and finance fields before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and cognee supports multiple instances with session memory. If both are pointed at the same mutable files or shared service state, they can overwrite each other’s work. No locking or shared-resource coordination is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared service state without locks, concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Run only one writer per shared resource.
Add a simple file lock around shared artifacts.
Snapshot state before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell/file actions, and cognee stores session memory and workflow patterns that may be reused downstream. If cognee treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into later decisions or workflows. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF cognee ingests AutoGPT-produced facts without verification, incorrect outputs can be reused.
IF downstream workflows act on stored memory automatically, one bad step can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before storing AutoGPT outputs.
Tag AutoGPT-derived records as untrusted.
Add validation rules for facts and citations.
Limit automatic reuse of newly written memory.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. If those data classes are processed through AutoGPT, residency, retention, or disclosure controls may diverge from cognee’s tenant-scoped handling. The profiles do not specify certifications or DPAs, so the compliance gap is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is copied from cognee into AutoGPT, retention and disclosure controls may differ.
IF AutoGPT sends those records to external services, residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from AutoGPT runs.
Use a DPA-approved environment only.
Log which records cross the boundary.
Delete temporary files after each run.
